page: Amazon Web Services c5n.18xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 72 vCPUs and 36 physical cores based on the x86_64 architecture, utilizing Intel Xeon 8124M processors running at 3.4 GHz. The system is equipped with 192.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 2.67 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage.

In benchmark testing, the instance demonstrates strong multi-core CPU performance, scoring 66660.83 in stress-ng multi-core tests and 49891.05 in PassMark CPU evaluations. Memory read bandwidth is also strong, reaching 3704.68 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 208.32 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. However, single-core performance and text generation for large language models are relatively weak, with LLM text generation for a 7B model averaging 7.23 tokens per second.

The instance features a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps, making it highly suitable for network-intensive workloads. Given the high vCPU count, strong multi-core capabilities, and lack of local storage, this server is well-suited for distributed computing, high-performance web serving, database operations, and multi-threaded decompression tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services c5n.18xlarge is a compute-optimized, network-optimized instance featuring 72 vCPUs and 36 physical cores powered by Intel Xeon 8124M processors at 3.4 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture and the Nitro hypervisor, it includes 192.0 GB of DDR4 memory but lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. The instance delivers strong multi-core CPU performance and high memory read bandwidth, supported by a 100 Gbps baseline network interface. While single-core speeds and LLM text generation performance are average to weak, its massive parallel processing power and high network throughput make it highly effective for network-heavy applications, multi-threaded data processing, database operations, and distributed compute workloads.
